ui.disclaimer: This is a document-drafting aid, not legal advice.
ui.review.title: Review your answers
ui.review.lead: Check the summary below, then generate your will. Tap any section to go back and change it.
ui.review.checklist.title: Before you finish
ui.review.checklist.lead: A few things a will alone can't finish:
ui.warning.noResiduary: You haven't set a residuary clause — anything not specifically listed in your will is governed by inheritance law, not your wishes.
ui.warning.muslimThird: As a Muslim testator, bequests beyond one-third of your net estate need your heirs' consent — your will already includes a clause reflecting this.
ui.checklist.nomination: Align the nomination on {asset} with this will.
ui.checklist.accessNote: Set up an access note for {asset} — without it, this wish may stall.
ui.checklist.digitalAccess: Create a digital access note (a sealed envelope or password manager's emergency access) — without it, most digital wishes stall.
ui.checklist.legacyTools: Set up each platform's own legacy tools now (Facebook Legacy Contact, Google Inactive Account Manager) — they act faster than a will.
ui.checklist.tellExecutor: Tell your executor they have been named, and where the signed will is kept.
ui.checklist.organRegister: Register your organ donor pledge (e.g. with NOTTO) and tell your family now — the will is usually read after the window for donation.
ui.checklist.bodyDonation: Body donation needs prior registration and family cooperation — arrange this now, not only in the will.
ui.signing.title: Signing & next steps
ui.signing.step1: Print single-sided, then sign every page.
ui.signing.step2: Sign in full at the end, before two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries (and ideally not your executor).
ui.signing.step3: Both witnesses should sign in your presence and in each other's presence, at the same time.
ui.signing.step4: A doctor's fitness certificate is optional but recommended for older testators — it helps pre-empt a sound-mind challenge later.
ui.signing.step5: Registration at the Sub-Registrar's office is optional, but strengthens the will as evidence.
ui.signing.step6: Store the signed original safely, and tell your executor exactly where it is.
ui.signing.step7: Review this will again after major life events — marriage, divorce, a birth, or a large purchase.
ui.signing.note: Stamp paper and notarisation are not required for a will in India.
